not.$comment: forbidden Realm authorship field; canonical name is created_by

security_class.description: Optional security class. 'high_assurance' forbids federation_policy=open and SHOULD use stricter resolver/E2EE/audit defaults. Omitted = 'standard'.

trust_domain.description: Immutable deployment trust domain captured by ck.realm.create. Receivers MUST require this to match the current Realm trust domain before accepting cross-domain replay-sensitive proofs.

fields.description: Product/profile fields. Security-relevant discriminators such as purpose=principal_control are schema constrained below; other product fields remain extension-defined.

relation_profiles.description: Optional Relation cardinality and conflict profiles declared by this Realm schema/profile.

on_conflict.description: Conflict handling for mutually unreachable Relation candidates. deterministic_winner selects the candidate with the bytewise-smallest canonical event_digest; it MUST NOT use HLC, actor id, local receive order, database id, or service insertion order.

preview_policy_id.description: Optional materialized pointer to the effective preview / peek policy. Canonical writes use ck.realm.preview_policy; absence means directory card / stripped state only, no history stub/snippet preview.

default_flow_id.description: Optional / nullable. AUTHORITATIVE single pointer to the Realm's default discussion Flow (last value projected from ck.realm.set_default_flow; cell ck.component.realm.set_default_flow.v1, cas_register, bottom=reject). A single pointer avoids multi-default dirty state. null / absent means the Realm has no designated default Flow. The reducer rejects a set_default_flow whose flow_id does not resolve to a projected non-tombstoned Flow in this Realm (failed_precondition), so this pointer never dangles. The Flow projection's derived is_default flag is computed as flow_id == this value; clients discover the default Flow deterministically from this field (or the Flow is_default marker) and MUST NOT rely on any Flow-reuses-Realm-UUID implementation detail. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md (default-Flow discovery).

content_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide content encryption floor (models/circle.md §7, models/realm-and-space.md §4). This is the Realm's actual content-encryption on/off switch. When e2ee_required, the effective_scope of Flow / Message / Morph / Blob content MUST be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS); reducer MUST failed_precondition (reason=content_encryption_floor_violation) on plaintext content. Independent of encryption_profile, which only declares the encryption MECHANISM (whether an MLS group exists), not which Cokret fields enter ciphertext. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with content_encryption_floor_downgrade. Defaults to allow_plaintext when absent.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide metadata encryption floor (models/circle.md §7), binary and symmetric with content_encryption_floor. allow_plaintext lets user-readable metadata stay wire-plaintext; e2ee_required forces it into encrypted_metadata. Comparison order allow_plaintext < e2ee_required. Effective floor = max(parent Realm value, Circle metadata floor, Space child_scope_policy floor, object profile requirement); any write below the effective floor MUST failed_precondition (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_violation). MUST NOT be relaxed by Circle, Space, or object profile. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade. When absent, reducers default to e2ee_required for mls_rfc9420 or content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required Realms, otherwise allow_plaintext.

agent_participation.description: Realm agent participation ceiling: { native_agent: { reply, accept_third_party_mention, act_on_behalf } } — the maximum native personal agent behavior permitted Realm-wide, written by a holder of ck.realm.admin via ck.realm.policy_components. It is the top of the deployment ⊇ Realm ⊇ Circle ⊇ Flow tighten-only chain (inner ceilings MUST NOT widen it; reducer rejects with agent_participation_ceiling_widen). When absent, inherits the deployment-default ceiling (deny-default under sovereign profiles). native_agent and applet_agent ceilings MUST be declared separately. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md.

sync_endpoints.description: Realm-level service binding list for shared notary / sync / mirror / federation peer surfaces. Directory resolve responses expose a requester-filtered join_candidates projection for join-side ingress; raw sync_endpoints are not a public candidate list. Member-level delivery_binding remains on ck.member.state and MUST NOT be inferred from this list.

notary_profile.description: Create-locked Seal finality profile. single_did and threshold deployments require signed Seal single-chain uniqueness; open_set deployments allow multiple Seal leaves and deterministic joined control views; mixed deployments use a primary notary plus fallback recovery notary.

digest_algorithm.description: Create-locked digest suite (canonicalization x hash tuple) used for DataEvent ids, Control Move ids, Seal ids, state_root, and Merkle leaves within this Realm. Defaults to sha256. Value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json (this enum MUST be regenerated when a row flips active, e.g. cbor.sha256); bare ids denote canonical-JSON canonicalization, dotted ids denote alternate canonical encodings. Exactly one live suite per Realm; migration uses a control-plane suite-transition Control Move finalized by Seal, see event-auth-state-resolution.md §4.2.5.

notary.description: Genesis value for the Realm notary cell. Subsequent changes are Control Moves finalized by the previous notary. For single_did profiles, recovery_members and controller organization evidence are required so reducer/authz can reject single-organization recovery setups.

forensic_attribution.$comment: Required for type=threshold (enforced by allOf below). MUST be quorum_intersection when 2*threshold > members.length (two conflicting quorums then intersect in at least one attributable double-signer; see authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1 and BFT Protocol Forensics). MUST be waived when 2*threshold <= members.length, declaring that automatic culprit attribution is unavailable. JSON Schema cannot compare threshold against members.length, so the arithmetic side is reducer/conformance validation (ck.vector.cba_lattice.threshold_forensic_attribution.v1).
forensic_attribution.description: Equivocation culprit-attribution mode for threshold notary committees: quorum_intersection (2k>n, automatic attribution available) or waived (k<=n/2, deployment explicitly waives automatic attribution and relies on committee-level handling).

controller_organization.description: DID of the organization controlling the primary notary, when the resolver or deployment policy can derive it. Required for single_did profile so recovery diversity can be verified.

recovery_controller_organizations.description: Organization DIDs controlling recovery_members. Reducer MUST verify at least one differs from controller_organization for single_did profile.

revocation_freshness_window_ms.description: Realm-level maximum control-plane seal distance/time window for accepting DataEvents whose seal_ref predates an observed revocation seal. Receivers evaluate this window by seal topology and policy, not by unverified event signing time. High-risk Realms SHOULD use a short value or move the affected cell family to control plane.

seal_compaction_max_interval_ms.description: Structural obligation, not advisory: maximum interval between compaction Seals (Seals carrying covered_event_digests[] or an equivalent verifiable full-coverage manifest). Because the cumulative control-plane covered set is defined recursively from predecessor_refs + delta, compaction Seals are the only bounded bootstrap points for new verifiers; a notary that exceeds this interval degrades bootstrap to walking the chain to genesis. open_set deployments MUST use <= 86400000 (24h); threshold deployments MUST use <= 604800000 (7d); single_did SHOULD use <= 86400000. Receivers SHOULD raise governance health alarms when the live chain exceeds the declared interval. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.2 and conformance vector ck.vector.cba_lattice.seal_compaction_interval_enforced.v1.

max_delegation_lifetime_ms.description: Realm-level maximum lifetime window used when an otherwise unbounded parent grant first delegates. Reducers freeze delegation_expiry_seal = first_delegation_sealed_at + effective max_delegation_lifetime_ms and MUST NOT refresh it on re-delegation. Effective value is the minimum of this field and any stricter grant, policy, deployment, or profile override. Defaults to 86400000 ms (24h). See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.1.

bottom_escalation_after_ms.description: Optional timeout after which unresolved bottom diagnostics should be escalated to recovery governance. Expiry does not choose a winner automatically.

cell_lattices.description: Optional Realm-specific lattice declarations for extension cell families.

co_write_policy.description: Optional whitelist constraining which cell families may be written by the same Move.

allOf.$comment: single_did notary profiles must declare an explicit recovery notary path at Realm create time. Distinct controlling organization is semantic/reducer validation because JSON Schema cannot compare DID-controller derivations across resolver evidence.

Threshold notary committees must declare their equivocation culprit-attribution mode at Realm create time. The arithmetic rule (quorum_intersection iff 2*threshold > members.length) is reducer/conformance validation; see notary.forensic_attribution $comment.

Principal control Realms are ordinary ck.schema.realm.v1 objects, but the profile discriminator must be closed at schema level: fields.purpose and schema_refs must appear together, the Realm MUST be MLS-backed, and both encryption floors MUST be pinned to e2ee_required (key-management §4.1 / §5.0.1, realm-and-space §2.8.1). There is no plaintext-floor PCR in v1.
The inverse guard prevents a profile-tagged Realm from omitting the machine-readable purpose discriminator, and pins the encryption floors symmetrically with the forward guard.

cell_role.description: Semantic role declared by Realm schema. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST NOT use lattice types lww_register or rga (enforced by allOf below). ui_affordance / content / draft / cosmetic MAY use lww_register or rga.

plane.description: CBA plane for this cell family. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST be control. Ordinary content / draft / cosmetic cells SHOULD be data unless sealed=true.

sealed.description: Opt-in control-plane finality for an otherwise data-like cell family. When true, plane MUST be control.

initial_value.description: Optional cell schema initial value (cas_register only). When defined, the cas_register `join` algorithm initialises `current` to this value (rather than null) before applying any Move. Combined with a `head_eq: <initial_value>` predicate on the first set Move, this implements singleton-once-set cells via the empty sentinel pattern. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.3.

sentinel_writers.description: Optional companion to `initial_value` (cas_register only). When `initial_value` is declared, set ops whose effect equals the sentinel are rejected by default (initial_value_reserved). Listing event_kinds here permits those event_kinds to write the sentinel back — typically the cleanup event_kind in a singleton-once-set / explicit-reset workflow. Capability authorization remains a separate independent check. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.3.

allOf.$comment: sealed=true is the explicit data-to-control opt-in.
initial_value is only defined for cas_register (see event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.3.3). Other lattices reject the field.

sentinel_writers is the companion of initial_value; it only makes sense on a cas_register cell that has declared initial_value. Reject declarations on other lattices, and reject declarations on cas_register cells that lack initial_value (since there is no sentinel to authorise writing back).
